findings.summary: The two new production subprocess runners execute the frozen acceptance with no timeout, unlike every other engine execution path (AcceptanceStage 1800s at dd_scripts.py:215-220, agent runs 3600s at dd_actors.py:406). The mutation gate is now armed by default on every final_review and calls _default_runner once per enumerated target, and a target deletion is precisely the kind of edit that can turn a bounded test into an unbounded one (removing a break, a timeout argument, a cancel/close call). A single hanging target wedges the final_review stage forever: MUTATION_EXECUTION_FAILED and the bounded-retry machinery the gate deliberately fails closed into are never reached, because subprocess.run never returns. Bounding both runners (and mapping the expiry onto the existing MUTATION_EXECUTION_FAILED path) would close it.

S12.5's checklist and S12.3's mutation receipt land in the engine-written sidecar (continuous/final-review-sidecar.json) rather than inside the sealed review.json. The judgment is that this is compliant, not a defect: the review-result schema is an external loop-engine plugin contract mirrored under dd/contracts with additionalProperties:false, the real sealer is the plugin (a new key would be a SCHEMA_VIOLATION at the seal, not a repairable nit), and the spec's boundary confines this order to the fleet-graph repo. Spec 8.3 names 'review.json 或其旁挂工件' as the receipt channel, and every red-able criterion passes: a findings==0 review without a checklist is refused INVALID_HANDOFF_SCHEMA at ingestion, and both phases' sidecars are asserted by test. Recorded so the divergence from the literal wording of criterion 2 ('review.json 工件必须含...') is on the record rather than passed over.

The receipt's read side is library-level: load_mutation_receipt is called by tests only, and handle_dd_awaiting_gate_wake still has no caller outside fleet_graph.self_gate in src/, so the sidecar-to-gate hop is performed by the goal-line agent rather than by a production Python module. This is not the defect the 12:4x tightening targeted -- that one was engine-side, and the final_review execution entry is now genuinely reachable from the single production assembly site -- and the gate fails closed on a missing receipt (duty_mutation_receipt refuses None, so no receipt can never mean a silent APPROVE). Flagged because it is the same shape as the wiring class S12 exists to catch, on the half of the loop M3 cannot exercise until it is on a real machine.

Verification-method caveat, recorded rather than passed over silently: this reviewer role has read-only file inspection and no shell/Git execution, so the mandated `git diff --exit-code 9db47f4a 7d3e7613 -- . ':(exclude).dev-dispatch'` was not run and no exit code is claimed for it. Product consistency was assessed by content inspection of the worktree: the only material present for 7d3e7613 beyond 9db47f4a is the reserved-namespace artifact .dev-dispatch/reviews/rc-d7eca50d-.../review.json plus its feedback/index.json entry, which is a compliant metadata-only materialization. The APPROVE above rests on the product code as read in the worktree, not on that check.
